subject: Acme Bank - region pinning & data residency follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: John Keller <john.keller@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Bank - region pinning & data residency follow-up

Thanks for taking the call earlier, John — good to meet you and Alice. Quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned on requirements and follow-ups:

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary requirement: customer data and inference processing for production customers must reside in the US (US-only region pinning) for the first phase.
- Cross-region failover is required for DR but failover must not result in EU/APAC data residency for PII.
- Retention: logs tied to request metadata can be retained for 90 days; audit logs need a longer retention (7 years) but must be exportable to your SIEM/KMS prior to deletion.
- Logging controls: need ability to mask PII in logs and an option to disable full request body retention for certain endpoints.

Open items / action items:
1) Can you confirm which types of data you classify as PII (names, email, account numbers, partial SSNs)? This will help us draft exact masking rules. (Action: John)
2) We’ll attach a short region-pinning design doc and SOC2 evidence stub for your security team to review. (Action: Aditya/Marissa)
3) Marissa will propose a failover design that ensures backups and DR run in a US region or to your designated DR VPC. (Action: Marissa)
4) Schedule follow-up tech session next week to walk through the proposed deployment and to validate retention/export flows. (Action: all)

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-overview.pdf, soc2-audit-evidence-stub.png

Proposed times for the follow-up: Tue 2027-04-06 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 2027-04-07 14:00-15:00 PT — let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

From: John Keller <john.keller@acmebank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmebank.com>, security@acmebank.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Bank - region pinning & data residency follow-up

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- PII definitions: yes — full name, email, national ID, account numbers, and any unmasked payment card data. Partial IDs (last 4 digits) are OK if explicitly permitted.
- Failover: we require automatic failover for availability but the failover target must be a US-only region controlled by Redwood or to our DR VPC (we prefer the former for operational simplicity).
- Backups: backups must be stored encrypted at rest in a US region. We need the option to hold encrypted snapshots for up to 1 year; short-term retention is fine for logs (90 days).
- Masking: must be configurable per-environment and per-route. Prefer an allowlist approach where only explicit fields are persisted.

We’ll have our security team (security@acmebank.com) review the docs. Please include any notes about key management (KMS/HSM) and whether Redwood can integrate with our KMS.

I’m available for the follow-up on Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PT. See you then.

—John
Director, Cloud Security
Acme Bank
john.keller@acmebank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Keller <john.keller@acmebank.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Bank - region pinning & data residency follow-up

John / team — thanks for the confirmations. A few technical notes and proposed approaches based on your requirements:

1) Region pinning model: Redwood supports explicit region pinning per-customer with an enforceable routing policy. For Acme Bank we can pin production inference and request storage to us-west-2 (US) and configure read-only replicas for metrics in a separate monitoring account if needed (still in US).

2) Cross-region failover & backups: we will implement active-active routing for throughput and an active-passive failover plan where the passive replica is also in a US region. Backups/snapshots will be encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys (we support AWS KMS and HSM integrations) and can be configured to remain in US-only S3 buckets. Snapshot retention up to 1 year is supported; we’ll add lifecycle rules to automatically expire older snapshots.

3) Logging & masking: Redwood’s logging pipeline supports field-level scrubbing via a per-route allowlist, and we can disable full request-body retention per environment. Audit logs (who/when/what) can be exported via secure S3 or pushed to your SIEM via our push connector. We will provide a short config sample in the doc.

4) SOC2 / evidence: attached is a minimal SOC2 evidence stub (soc2-audit-evidence-stub.png) and the high-level design doc (redwood-region-pinning-overview.pdf). These are intended for initial review — we can provide more artifacts under NDA if your team needs them.

Next steps I’ll take before the call on Tue 2027-04-06:
- Produce a draft mutual action plan and a config sample showing how to pin to us-west-2 and enforce masking rules.
- Draft a KMS integration note with the steps for onboarding your key.

If John or security team has any blockers on the KMS approach or backup location, please flag them and we’ll adjust.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
